title: Complete reducibility for semisimple algebraic groups in characteristic zero
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $G$ be a semisimple $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup; solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial. A rational $G$-module is an $F$-vector space $V$ with a coaction $V\to V\otimes_F F[G]$ satisfying coassociativity and the counit identity. A submodule is a linear subspace whose coaction takes values in its tensor product with $F[G]$. Simple means nonzero with no proper nonzero submodule. Equivariance means a coaction identity, equivalently equivariance after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Assume $\operatorname{char}F=0$. Every finite-dimensional rational $G$-module is a finite direct sum of simple rational $G$-submodules (the empty sum is allowed for $V=0$).

source.place: Section 22c, Proposition 22.41, printed p.477; characteristic zero is the standing hypothesis of Section 22c on p.475.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-semisimple-characters-trivial], every character of $G$ is trivial. Apply [lem-sfb-simple-hyperplane-splitting-criterion]: it remains to prove that, for every finite-dimensional rational $G$-module $U$ and every simple submodule $W$ with $\dim_F(U/W)=1$, $W$ has a rational complement. This criterion requires an affine finite-type group and the same coaction notion of rational module, exactly as here.

source.place: Lemma 22.40, printed pp.476-477; Proposition 22.41, first reduction

proof.text: Fix such $U,W$. If the action on $U$ is trivial, extend a basis of $W$ by one vector: its span is a rational complement because every subspace has coaction $v\mapsto v\otimes1$. Otherwise [lem-sfb-semisimple-group-casimir-trace] supplies a $G$-equivariant $c=c_U$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_U(c)=n\cdot1_F$, $n>0$, and preserving $W$. The one-dimensional rational module $U/W$ is a character (in a basis its action is an invertible scalar), hence trivial by [lem-sfb-semisimple-characters-trivial]. The trivial-quotient clause of the Casimir node therefore gives $c(U)\subseteq W$.

source.place: Proposition 22.41, printed p.477; Casimir construction on pp.475-476

proof.text: The simple module $W$ is nonzero. Apply [lem-zl-alg-closed-endomorphism-eigenvalue] to $c|_W$ to obtain $a\in F$ with nonzero eigenspace. Equivariance of $c$ makes $\ker(c|_W-a\,1_W)$ a rational submodule: its coaction identity follows by applying $c-a$ to the first tensor factor, and tensoring vector spaces over $F$ preserves kernels. Simplicity forces this eigenspace to equal $W$, so $c|_W=a\,1_W$. In a basis of $W$ extended to $U$, $c(U)\subseteq W$ gives a block matrix with diagonal blocks $aI_W$ and $0$. Thus $a\dim_F W=\operatorname{Tr}_U(c)=n\cdot1_F\ne0$, using characteristic zero. In particular $a\ne0$.

source.place: Proposition 22.41, printed p.477 (Schur step written as an eigenspace argument)

proof.text: Regard $p=a^{-1}c$ as a map $U\to W$. It is equivariant and $p|_W=1_W$. Its kernel $L$ is rational by the coaction identity, and every $u\in U$ has the decomposition $u=p(u)+(u-p(u))$ with $p(u)\in W$ and $u-p(u)\in L$; also $W\cap L=0$. Hence $U=W\oplus L$. This verifies the criterion's antecedent for every $U,W$, so [lem-sfb-simple-hyperplane-splitting-criterion] gives the claimed finite simple decomposition. The zero module has its empty decomposition.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 22.41, via Lemma 22.40 and the Casimir construction of Section 22c, printed pp.475-477
